title: Traffic smoothing, quiet-hours and tenant notification playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines operator and customer-facing procedures for smoothing traffic during predictable and ad-hoc tenant burst events. It covers automatic quiet-hours smoothing, tenant-level throttling/fan-out controls, notification templates, escalation ladders, telemetry queries, and rollback guidance. The goal is to preserve platform SLOs (latency/availability) while protecting customer experience and cost boundaries.

When to use this playbook:

- Planned quiet-hours or maintenance windows where we will intentionally reduce tenant throughput to conserve capacity or schedule upgrades.
- Rapid tenant traffic bursts (spikes in requests or tokens) that threaten SLOs for other tenants.
- Customer-requested temporary throttle during migration/backfill events.
- As a standard operating response prior to capacity augmentation or emergency capacity scaling.

Key objectives:

1) Maintain 99th percentile p95 token latency SLOs and >99.9% availability for host-level API endpoints.
2) Minimize customer-facing error rate and provide clear, timely communication.
3) Apply smoothing/throttles with least possible disruption using automated, observable controls.

Ownership and roles:

- Primary owner: Customer Success Operations (Customer Success) — coordinates customer comms, approves manual throttles.
- Secondary owner: Platform SRE (Engineering) — implements rate-limiter changes, monitors platform metrics, executes emergency capacity procedures.
- Response lead (oncall): person listed on the current oncall rota for Eng SRE.

Preconditions / prerequisites:

- Tenant must have telemetry forwarding enabled (tenant.metrics and tenant.traces).
- Tenant-specific quota and throttle policies must exist in the RateLimit Service (service: rate-limit-svc).
- Customer Success must have an agreed contact from the tenant (email + pager for enterprise).

SLOs and thresholds (operational):

| Metric | Threshold (trigger) | Severity | Initial action | Escalation timer |
|-------|---------------------:|----------|----------------|------------------|
| p95 token latency (global) | > 1.8x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes | Sev-2 | Auto-smooth tenants contributing >30% load | 10 min -> SRE oncall |
| error rate (5xx >= host) | >0.5% absolute increase over baseline (5 min) | Sev-1 | Immediate rollback of recent config + alert | 5 min -> Incident page |
| requests-per-min per-tenant | > 10x baseline sustained 2 min | Sev-3 | Apply per-tenant burst windowing + backpressure | 15 min -> CS PD notification |

Automated controls and tuning knobs:

- Quiet-hours smoothing: schedule-based traffic shaping that lowers max active concurrent requests by x% (default 30%) during predefined windows. Config stored as YAML in config-store:

  examples: &config-example
  - tenant_selector: "label:batching=true"
    window: "23:00-05:00 UTC"
    concurrency_limit_pct: 70
    burst_window_seconds: 60

- Tenant burst windowing: dynamic token-bucket policy applied per-API key that allows short bursts but enforces an average over a sliding 60s window.

- Graceful response headers: when rate-limited, return 429 with headers: Retry-After, X-Redwood-Limit, X-Redwood-Remaining, X-Redwood-Quota-Reset. Include optional human-readable JSON in body with guidance on next steps.

Telemetry & queries (examples):

- Grafana / Prometheus:
  - redwood.requests_total{tenant_id=~"<TENANT>"}
  - redwood.tokens_per_minute{tenant_id=~"<TENANT>"}
  - redwood.p95_token_latency{region="us-west-2"}
  - redwood.5xx_rate{host="api.redwood.com"}

- Example PromQL:
  avg_over_time(redwood.tokens_per_minute{tenant_id=~"T123"}[2m]) > 10 * avg_over_time(redwood.tokens_per_minute{tenant_id=~"T123"}[1h])

Operational runbook (step-by-step):

1) Detect: automated alert or CS report. Confirm tenant_id(s), time window, and affected routes.
2) Quick triage (5 min): verify telemetry, check deploys in last 30 min (ci-cd activity), confirm whether traffic is legitimate (backfill / scheduled job).
3) Apply automated smoothing if hit threshold: enable "quiet-hours smoothing" for tenant selector or apply per-tenant rate-limit override. Use CLI:

  # apply per-tenant override (example)
  rwctl rate-limit set --tenant T123 --max-rps 250 --burst 500 --window 60s --reason "auto-smoothing-trigger-2027-02-15"

4) Notify customer: send templated email and optional in-console banner (see templates below). Mark the change in incident tracker with runbook link.
5) Monitor 0-30 minutes: watch p95 latency, 5xx rate, and tenant error rates. If metrics improve, prepare staged rollback: reduce throttle by 20% every 10 minutes until normal.

Escalation matrix and timers:

- If p95 latency not improved after 15 minutes -> escalate to Eng SRE oncall (page) and SRE escalation Slack channel (#sre-incident).
- If 5xx error rate increases after smoothing -> immediate rollback and incident page start.
- If customer reports data loss or persistent functional errors -> raise Sev-1 and schedule cross-team warroom.

Customer communications (templates):

- In-console banner (short):
  "We are applying temporary traffic smoothing to maintain platform performance during a high-volume event. Your requests may be delayed or throttled. We will update you within 30 minutes. Contact support@redwood.ai for urgent concerns."

- Email template (first notification):
  Subject: Temporary traffic smoothing active for your Redwood tenant

  Hello <Customer Name>,

  We detected a high-volume traffic event affecting your Redwood tenant (ID: <TID>). To maintain platform stability, we've temporarily limited peak throughput for your tenant. This is a protective measure — your data is not at risk. Expected impact: brief 429s for short bursts and up-to-30s increased latency for long requests.

  What we are doing: applying per-tenant smoothing, monitoring performance, and escalating if needed.

  ETA for update: 30 minutes. Contact: <CS rep + pager>.

  Regards,
  Redwood Support

- Follow-up template (when resolved):
  Subject: Traffic smoothing removed — event resolved

  Hello <Customer Name>,

  The temporary smoothing has been removed and your normal throughput limits restored. Incident runbook: <link>. If you observed any functional problems, please reply and we will investigate further.

Configuration table (required fields for a scheduled quiet-hours rule):

| Field | Type | Description | Example | Required |
|-------|------|-------------|---------|----------:|
| rule_id | string | Unique rule identifier | quiet-window-batch | yes |
| tenant_selector | string | Selector expression (labels or tenant_id) | label:batching=true | yes |
| window | string | Time window in UTC | 23:00-05:00 | yes |
| concurrency_limit_pct | integer | Percent of normal concurrency to allow | 70 | yes |
| burst_window_seconds | integer | Sliding window for burst smoothing | 60 | no |
| owner | string | Team/owner to notify | customer-success | yes |

Rollback guidance:

- If smoothing causes unacceptable customer errors, immediately remove rule and clear rate-limit overrides using rwctl:

  rwctl rate-limit delete --tenant T123 --reason "rollback-due-to-5xx-2027-02-15"

- If rollback triggers platform instability, revert to platform-wide safe-mode throttle (config: global.safe_mode_pct = 50) and open incident page.

Post-incident actions and reporting:

1) Run a 72-hour retrospective: who acted, what thresholds fired, and whether automation behaved as expected.
2) Produce a short incident digest for the Customer (one-pager) within 48 hours.
3) Update the tenant onboarding checklist with any gap identified (telemetry, contact, agreed quiet-hours).

Observability checklist (what to capture):

- Alert triggers and timestamps.
- rwctl commands executed (audit log).
- Grafana snapshot links and PromQL used.
- Customer comms artifacts (email, banner text).

Related runbooks and docs:

- Capacity surge and degraded throughput playbook (eng/sre)
- Tenant onboarding acceptance testing (CS)
- Rate limit service configuration guide (infra)

Appendix A — Example rate-limit YAML snippet:

  - rule_id: "quiet-window-batch-2027"
    tenant_selector: "label:batching=true"
    window: "23:00-05:00"
    concurrency_limit_pct: 70
    burst_window_seconds: 60
    owner: "customer-success"

Appendix B — Short checklist for CS before applying manual throttle:

1) Confirm authorized contact and approval in CRM.
2) Validate telemetry and rule selector matches intended workload.
3) Log expected duration and rollback criteria to incident tracker.
4) Send pre-action notice to customer.
